elements.element: Customer is not subject to any restriction on soliciting the other party’s personnel.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that “neither party will solicit,” thereby binding Customer/Licensee.

elements.element: The non-solicitation obligation is mutual and applies symmetrically to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause applies to “neither party” and protects employees of each party from solicitation by the other.

elements.element: The restriction applies only to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: The clause covers employees directly involved in “the performance of this Agreement,” which may extend beyond personnel directly involved in the services.

elements.element: The restriction ends twelve months after each covered person’s involvement in the services ends.
elements.evidence: The clause runs during the entire Agreement term and for twelve months after expiration or termination, rather than measuring the period from the end of each person’s involvement. It may therefore last substantially longer than twelve months after an individual’s involvement ends.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from solicitation.
elements.evidence: The definition expressly excludes “generally advertising job openings” and follow-up with individuals who respond to those advertisements.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by personnel are excluded from solicitation.
elements.evidence: The definition excludes activities involving individuals who “voluntarily initiate employment inquiries.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring personnel who are otherwise lawfully contacted.
elements.evidence: The operative restriction prohibits solicitation to leave employment but does not independently prohibit hiring or employing an individual.

result.reason: The redline appropriately makes the restriction mutual, reduces the stated post-term period to twelve months, preserves the advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs, and adds no no-hire restriction. It nevertheless fails the fallback because its scope is tied to performance of the Agreement rather than expressly to the services, and—more importantly—the twelve-month period runs from expiration or termination of the Agreement rather than from the end of each individual’s involvement. Customer also remains bound, so the preferred position is not met.
